beats.narration_en: Same puddle, same speed. Only one car can still steer.
Those grooves are drains that squeeze water out from under the tire.
New tires have about eight millimeters of them.
Worn to the legal limit, just one point six.
Then the water can't escape fast enough.
It piles up into a wedge and lifts the tire off the road.
Now you're water skiing. Steering and brakes barely work.
NASA even has a rule of thumb for when it starts.
Nine times the square root of your tire pressure gives the speed in miles per hour.
At thirty two psi that's about fifty, and worn tires float even sooner.
Check yours with a penny. If you can see the top of Lincoln's head, it's time.
If you start to float, ease off the gas and keep the wheel straight until the tires bite again.
